title: Iconic, rare, endemic and threatened: macroecological insights to support conservation and management of Primula palinuri
abstract: Abstract Primula palinuri Petagna is a narrow endemic species confined to Tyrrhenian coastal cliff habitats in southern Italy and threatened by climate change and anthropogenic pressures. We assessed the current, past and future habitat suitability of P. palinuri in Italy using a macroecological framework based on ecological niche modelling and GIS analyses. Furthermore, focusing on the present distribution, we conducted a conservation gap analysis to quantify the proportion of suitable habitat included within protected areas. Our models identified precipitation of the driest and wettest months, annual temperature range and distance from limestone substrates and grazing areas as the main contributors to model performance. The highest suitability values were concentrated around Palinuro (currently the area with the greatest population density) and along the southern Cilento region. Additionally, projections highlighted two geographically isolated areas outside the calibration range—Liguria and Tuscany—as potentially suitable for the occurrence of P. palinuri . Conservation gap analysis revealed that 41% of the predicted suitable habitat lies outside protected areas. Paleoclimatic projetcions indicated a significant expansion of climatically suitable areas during the Last Glacial Maximum, while showed a marked range contraction throughout the Last Interglacial and Mid-Holocene. Future climate projections (2040–2100) consistently predicted a marked reduction in suitable habitat, irrespective of the emission scenario considered. Overall, our results underscore the high vulnerability of P. palinuri to ongoing climatic and land-use changes and emphasise the urgent need for integrated conservation strategies to ensure its long-term persistence.
problem: Effective conservation of the rare endemic plant *Primula palinuri* is challenged by its high vulnerability to climate change and anthropogenic pressures, necessitating a comprehensive assessment of its past, present, and future habitat suitability to address gaps in protection and ensure its long-term survival.
method: This paper proposes a macroecological framework using ecological niche modelling and GIS analyses to assess the current, past, and future habitat suitability of the endemic plant *Primula palinuri* to inform its conservation and management strategies.
task: The task is to assess the current, past, and future habitat suitability of the endemic plant *Primula palinuri* in Italy using ecological niche modelling and GIS analyses to support its conservation and management.
innovation: This paper provides the first spatially explicit, macroecological assessment of the factors shaping the distribution of *Primula palinuri* across past, present, and future scenarios, revealing its vulnerability to climate change and identifying key areas for its conservation.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: Its narrow, fragmented distribution makes it highly vulnerable to climate changes, habitat degradation and anthropogenic pressures, including cliff stabilization, tourism, infrastructure development, illegal collection and grazing (e.g., Aronne et al. 2014; Gangale et al. 2013; Uzunov et al. 2008). These areas are also subject to landslide risks due to geological instability and exposure to extreme weather (Gangale et al. 2013).

Our analyses revealed that P. palinuri occurs in Mediterranean habitats characterised by low annual precipitation and strong seasonal variability, consistent with its classification within arid bioclimatic zones (Pesaresi et al. 2017).
